rules.note: LOCKED team layer: reading secrets — credential files, secret stores, environment secrets — is never part of a coding job the agent may do itself, for any initiator, ever. A human handles secrets by hand, outside the agent.
LOCKED team layer: a force push rewrites shared history and can destroy other people's work; the agent never does it, for any initiator, ever. If history must be rewritten, a human does it by hand.

LOCKED team layer: anything classified DELETE — deleting a branch, and any other deletion — is refused. Deletions are hard to undo and outside the agent's standing brief; a human deletes by hand if it must happen.

Deploying or publishing a release puts code in front of users under the owner's name; it routes to the owner instead of executing or asking this run's approver. The owner ships it, or explicitly hands the release back.

Pushing to a remote and merging a pull request both change shared state other people build on, so they ask a human first, on the exact recorded payload. A normal (non-force) push asks — it is not denied, and it is not free.

Standing approval, bounded to exactly these kinds: running the project's tests and builds. A coding agent that must ask to run tests cannot work; test/build output stays local, and anything the build wants to do beyond EXECUTE is classified and judged separately.

Standing approval for local project work: writing and editing project files, and committing locally (git.commit is classified WRITE_LOCAL in this pack — a local commit is reversible and not yet shared). The verdict is pre_approved, not allow: the standing approval is recorded as such. Pushing the commit asks (push-and-merge-ask).
Reading, searching, grepping, and listing project code are free for every initiator, including unattended routines — understanding the codebase is the agent's day job.
